summary.headline: Jagsonpal Q1 FY27 revenue rose about 9% YoY to Rs.82 crores, with operating EBITDA up 21% to nearly Rs.19 crores and PAT up 22% to Rs.13 crores.
summary.overview: Management said the growth seen from Q4 FY26 carried into Q1 FY27, with revenue up about 9% YoY and gross margin above 65%. Operating EBITDA margin expanded about 240 bps to above 23% and PAT margin rose 176 bps to 16%. The company completed the Rs.40 crore buyback and acquired 85% of Aequitas Healthcare for Rs.20.8 crores (enterprise value about Rs.25 crores) to enter the hospital segment. Management guided Aequitas to Rs.10 crores EBITDA by year two post-integration, though analysts questioned the step-up from about Rs.50 lakh EBITDA in FY26.

financial_highlights.change: after Rs.40 crore buyback (about half added back to cash)

segments.name: Branded prescription (core)
segments.commentary: Power brand portfolio grew 19% vs market 16%; five brands are #1 in their molecules and 14 are in the top five. Maintane (Pharmarack ~Rs.46 crores: injections Rs.34 crores, tablets Rs.13 crores) is one of the top three brands. Management is shifting mix from acute to semi-chronic and specialty therapies; new brand run-rates have almost doubled.

segments.name: Aequitas Healthcare (hospital pharma, 85% owned)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs.53 crores and EBITDA about Rs.50 lakh per analyst. Portfolio is ICU and perioperative injectables, including latest-generation antibiotics, all branded, sold to corporate hospital chains (no government tenders). Management targets about Rs.100 crores revenue in FY28-FY29 and Rs.10 crores+ EBITDA by year two; gross margins are structurally thinner than JPL's branded business.

guidance_outlook: Target to grow at 1.5x industry growth rate in coming quarters (management reiterated on Pharmarack vs secondary-sales variance question).
Aequitas: about Rs.100 crores business within two and a half years (FY28-FY29) and Rs.10 crores+ EBITDA by year two post-integration; synergies expected over 36 months.
Productivity target of upward of Rs.2,50,000 per-person productivity (PCPM varies by vertical).
Dividend of 200% recommended, including 75% special dividend, subject to AGM approval.
Aequitas expected to contribute meaningfully from second year onwards; numbers expected to show in about the next two quarters.
capex_capacity: Aequitas acquired as a subsidiary (not a BTA route); working capital cycle is longer than JPL and will not be aligned with JPL.
Aequitas network: about 49 institutional medical representatives, access to over 1,000 hospitals, around 50 hospitals contribute the majority of top line.
Lean and green productivity programme rolled out company-wide in Q1.
demand_pricing: Secondary (Pharmarack) growth of 18.9% vs reported primary sales growth of about 9%; management attributed the gap to stockist data and geographic statistical correction, and said it is reviewing the variance.
Hospital channel pricing is price-led; management said margins are structurally thinner than in branded prescription business.
Top 10 Aequitas products are over 50% of its sales.
Management reported one first-wave product launch in Q1 and expects one more in the current quarter.
Brand focus for growth: Indocap, Maintane, Endoreg (gynae), Pru and Eukroma (derma).

qa_highlights.question: Why is reported sales growth (about 9%) far below the 18% IPM growth cited?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the data is secondary (stockist) sales and the variance is partly statistical correction for geographies; it is reviewing why the gap is so wide and reiterated the 1.5x industry growth target.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Aequitas Rs.10 crore EBITDA target achievable from Rs.50 lakh in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited brand equity, lean team, corporate-chain focus, cross-selling of JPL brands and new-age brands with high value per patient; promoters remain with 15% and continue to run the business, so their salaries are not a one-off saving.

qa_highlights.question: Size of Maintane and its impact on portfolio growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Pharmarack value about Rs.46 crores (Rs.34 crores injections, Rs.13 crores tablets); growing ahead of molecule market; one of top three brands, but management did not disclose internal values.

qa_highlights.question: Aequitas gross margin looks low for a branded business; why?
qa_highlights.answer: In hospitals, price comes before brand, so margins are thinner; management plans mix improvement and differentiated innovative launches, but said it is too early to quantify.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp working capital improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to inventory control and stricter collections, and said payments now go out on due date; the big step-down was in FY22-FY24 (cash conversion cycle from 59 to 22 days).

qa_highlights.question: Any first-in-India or breakthrough molecule pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it never mentioned such a pipeline; it is targeting first-wave launches (about 5-10 companies) in gynae, ortho and derma, and launched one such product in Q1.

risks_watch: Aequitas execution: hospital working capital is longer and margins thinner; Rs.10 crore EBITDA in year two is an aggressive target from Rs.50 lakh base.
Concentration risk: Maintane and Indocap drive much of recent growth; management acknowledges the portfolio effect depends on a few brands.
Gap between secondary (Pharmarack ~18.9%) and reported primary growth (~9%) needs explanation next quarter.
Attrition and sales-force productivity: management claims improvement but gave no hard numbers.
Board change: Pallavi Dinodia Gupta stepped down; Anil Kumar Matai joined as Independent Director.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and on the Aequitas thesis, but evasive on specifics: declined to give Maintane MAT value, exact PCPM, and the reason for the primary-versus-secondary sales gap, and said it is still too early to judge Aequitas margins.
key_quotes: This 9% growth in sales has translated into a 21% growth in operating EBITDA as well as a 22% growth in net profits for the company.
Aequitas alone, we are looking at around Rs.100 crores of business within two and a half years' time, starting from now.
Growth without margins, improvement is hollow.
